messages:
ira: heads-up — after the overnight driver/kmod push to 535.60 we're seeing intermittent peer-discovery flips that force NCCL into SOCKET/NET fallback on a subset of H100 racks :eyes:

sanjay: seen this on one rack in us-east-1b, two jobs dropped to ~50% throughput and latency spiked. logs show repeated 'ring can't find connected peer' followed by fallback message.

alex: logs? can you paste the nccl debug snippet?

ira: pasted below (redacted ids)
```
[2025-06-09 03:12:11] nccl-net: peer 10.8.21.45 -> link DOWN, falling back to SOCKET
[2025-06-09 03:12:11] nccl-kv: kvcache mismatch detected for peermap entry 3
[2025-06-09 03:12:11] nvlink-probe: nvlink detected=1 topo_mask=0x4 -> toggled to 0
[2025-06-09 03:12:12] nccl-shm: cannot allocate ipc handle, fallback to net
```

karen: interesting that nvlink flag toggles. These nodes are mixed: a-gpu-sku h100v3 + a older h100p variant (same family but different firmware). could be firmware/kernel interaction.

sanjay: repro steps so far: launch a bidirectional ncclAllReduce across 8 GPUs spanning two nodes (1x h100v3, 1x h100p), run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. cost: immediate fallback sometimes after ~6-12k tokens of KV cache growth.

alex: note: our serving runtime uses KV cache sharding across peers. if peermap hash differs, kvcache handshake fails and triggers SHM/TCP fallback to avoid stopping work. that explains throughput drop.

sre-oncall: any kernel or module changes in the rollout besides driver 535.60?

ira: kernel is 6.1.70 -> 6.1.75 on that fleet. also nvidia-uvm and nv_peer_mem had rebuilds. tried repro on a fully homogeneous h100v3 set — no issue. problem manifests on mixed-firmware/driver combinations.

karen: can we confirm whether the nvlink probe ordering race is due to module init order? maybe nvlink shows up briefly then disappears when udev settles.

alex: quick check: run `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` after repro. also check `/sys/class/nvlink/*/status`.

ira: ran those. see transient "NVLINK link is down" messages right before the peermap mismatch. attaching snippet to ticket.

sanjay: workaround idea: force NCCL to prefer SHM when peers are local using `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=none`? but that might be risky cross-node. Also we can set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to avoid NVLINK reliance for now.

alex: if we force-disable p2p then we lose the kvcache fast-path; throughput hits will be significant. Need a targeted rollback of the driver or kernel on the affected mixed-pair racks.

ira: propose immediate steps:
- pause driver rollout for mixed-hardware pools (rollback in canary completed) :no_entry_sign:
- create a narrow repro job that toggles kvcache growth to reproduce quickly
- collect full nccl debug logs + dmesg + /proc/modules on affected nodes
- open vendor escalation with NVIDIA (include firmware versions and kernel diff)

karen: I'll flag the ops runbook and mark the two AZ racks as cordoned from driver updates.

deploy-bot: deploy rollback started on pool h100-crosssku-canary at 2025-06-09T06:00Z :rocket:

sre-oncall: thanks. also add a cost note: jobs that fallback to socket spike egress and CPU consumption; watch the nightly cost dashboard for us-east-1b.

ira: adding: suspected root cause is nvlink discovery race combined with kvcache handshake being brittle across firmware mismatch. we should consider a small NCCL patch that tolerates transient peer toggles during handshake. will file an RFC and follow up with a patch queue. :memo:

alex: agreed. for now, hold upgrades for mixed-hardware shard and roll out driver+kernel together after vendor signoff. :thumbsup:
